## Restore-detection matrix

The adapter compares the cluster's system identifier and the timeline it is writing WAL on with the values recorded in the namespace record. "Detected" means the namespace read `quarantined` with no operator action.

| Event | System identifier changed | Timeline changed | Detected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Promotion of a streaming standby (suite D) | no | yes (1 to 2) | yes, on the first call |
| pg_dump restored into a fresh cluster (initdb) | yes | no | yes |
| pg_dump restored into the same cluster (another database, or the same one) | no | no | **no** |
| pg_basebackup + WAL archive, recovery_target_name, promote (PITR) | no | yes | yes |
| pg_basebackup copy (or a file-system snapshot) started without recovery.signal | no | no | **no** |
| Restart or crash recovery of the same cluster (suite C) | no | no | not a restore: the namespace keeps serving |

After the promotion in suite D, `pg_control_checkpoint().timeline_id` kept the old timeline for 269.6 s. The adapter reads the WAL insert timeline instead, which had changed on the first call.
